messages.author: ce683b307e5b88d5
messages.subject: NAs after protein group comparison
parts:
Dear MSstats developer team,
I have to do a power analysis on a pilot study in order to plan the real study.
It is DIA data analyzed in DIA-NN and I manually brought the data in 10 column format.

When I run the proteingroupcomparison I only get NAs for FCs pVals etc.

After dataprocess, the Abundance values were calculated, so I am not sure where the problem lies. 

I had the same problem before and Mateusz found that my annotation was wrong, so here I already checked the annotation twice for double annotated bioreplicates and even changed the bioreplicates in the data to make sure, there is no problem with the assignment of 
Condition <-> BioReplicate

I set up a really small reproducible sample, which I will attach.

Best, Klemens

messages.author: ce683b307e5b88d5
messages.subject: Re: NAs after protein group comparison
parts:
I cannot attach the R script. Here is the script for the example:


#packages
library(MSstats)

#set working directory to current folder of R script
setwd(dirname(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path))


# input
test2 <-  readRDS(file = "test.rds")


##### msstats analysis ######
msstats_dataprocess <- MSstats::dataProcess(raw = test2,
  normalization = F,
  MBimpute = F)

#investigate this
msstats_dataprocess$ProcessedData %>% View()

#contrast.matrix for comparison
comparison <-  data.frame(V1 = 1, V2 = -1)
colnames(comparison) <- levels(msstats_dataprocess$ProcessedData$GROUP_ORIGINAL)
rownames(comparison) <- c("Group.A vs Group.B")

msstats_comparison <- MSstats::groupComparison(data = msstats_dataprocess, contrast.matrix = comparison)

msstats_comparison$ComparisonResult %>% View()

if you change the way you create comparison matrix to

> matrix(c(1, -1), nrow = 1, ncol = 2)

will it solve the problem? I  just tested that on older R version and it worked.

I can add a check for class of contrast.matrix parameter. It's hard to catch all possible errors, though, and error message are not always helpful. (That was the case here - it's way it took me some time).
I'll see what I can do.


Kind regards,
Mateusz
